1.explanation: The core of the issue is in format-reveal.ts, where the code writes out the Reveal.initialize call. It currently interpolates the width and height options directly into the JS object without quoting string values. When width/height contain a '%' sign they must be emitted as quoted strings in JavaScript (e.g. width: "100%"), otherwise the script syntax is broken. metadata.ts defines the schema for these options but does not handle string conversion. Both files are implicated: format-reveal.ts must conditionally wrap percent values in quotes, informed by the metadata definitions in metadata.ts.
1.bug_scenario: When a user specifies width and height as percentage values (e.g. "100%") in their revealjs format options, the generated HTML’s initialization script emits unquoted values (width: 100%, height: 100%) which is invalid JavaScript (interpreted as modulus) and causes the presentation to fail to load (blank screen). Using numeric pixel values works because they produce valid JS (width: 1600, height: 900).

2.explanation:
• src/format/reveal/format-reveal.ts is responsible for reading the user’s `width`/`height` options and passing them along as Pandoc `-V` template variables. It currently assumes numeric values and emits them unquoted, so a value like `"100%"` gets coerced or dropped and never shows up correctly in the HTML style block.

• src/format/reveal/metadata.ts defines the TypeScript interface for Reveal.js options (including `width` and `height`) but types them as numbers. As a result string values (with "%") aren’t recognized or preserved.

• src/format/reveal/schemas.ts supplies the JSON schema for those same options, currently declaring `width`/`height` as numeric fields. Percent‐based string values are rejected or coerced away here.

Together these three files mean that any percentage‐based dimensions never make it into the final `<div class="reveal" style="width:…;height:…">` tag in the HTML; updating them to accept strings (and to emit quoted values when passing into the template) will restore correct percentage sizing.
2.bug_scenario: When you author a Reveal.js slide deck in Quarto and specify a percentage width/height (for example `width: "100%"` and `height: "100%"`) the rendered presentation comes up as a blank (black) screen. If you switch to numeric pixel values (for example `width: 1600`, `height: 900`), everything works. The underlying problem is that Quarto’s code that maps your `width`/`height` settings into the Pandoc template treats them as numbers and emits them without the necessary quotes or string‐type handling, so any trailing “%” is lost or mis-injected into the template and the Reveal.js container never sizes properly.
